page-upgrades-bug-bounty-client-bugs-des: The Quantaureum node software, its consensus logic, and the QVM execution engine must follow the protocol specification and be secure against network-level attacks.
Bugs that break consensus, allow theft of funds, or compromise validator keys are rewarded at the highest severity.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-clients-type-1: Consensus, QPOS or GM-QTD logic deviations that could split the network
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-clients-type-2: Unexpected crashes, remote code execution or denial of service in the node software
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-clients-type-3: Post-quantum signature (Dilithium3) or key encapsulation (Kyber768) implementation flaws
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-misc-bugs-desc: The official SDKs (Go, Rust, C++, Java, Python, TypeScript) and the qauctl tooling are in scope of the bug bounty program. Please include all details necessary to reproduce the vulnerability.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-misc-bugs-desc-: SDK bugs that could lead developers to construct unsafe transactions or mishandle key material are rewarded. Crashes of developer tools without security impact are tracked as normal issues.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-deposit-bugs-de: The validator staking flow (deposits, delegation, withdrawals) and the Merkle bridge specifications and source code are part of the bug bounty program.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-dependency-bugs: Certain dependencies are crucial for the Quantaureum network to function. Bugs in the cryptographic libraries that could weaken signature or encryption guarantees are rewarded at high severity.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-hunting-desc: The bug bounty program is a discretionary rewards program for the Quantaureum community. It supports our responsible-disclosure policy: vulnerabilities must be reported privately, fixed, and only then disclosed publicly.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-hunting-li-1: Report privately to security@quantaureum.com - never open a public GitHub issue for a vulnerability
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-hunting-li-2: Include steps to reproduce if possible
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-hunting-li-3: We acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and give an initial assessment within 7 days
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-hunting-li-4: Please do not disclose the vulnerability publicly until a fix is released
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-ledger-desc: The Quantaureum specifications detail the design rationale for consensus, execution, and the cryptography stack.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-meta-descriptio: The Quantaureum bug bounty program: how to report vulnerabilities privately, response timelines, and rewards paid in QAU by severity.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-not-included-de: Only the targets listed under in-scope are part of the Bug Bounty Program. Reports that do NOT qualify:
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-subtitle: Earn up to 5,000 QAU per vulnerability from a capped fund of 25,000 QAU by finding protocol, node and cryptographic implementation bugs affecting the Quantaureum network.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-type-2: QVM / QASM execution and JIT compiler bugs
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-type-3: P2P networking and protocol handling bugs
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-validity-desc: The bug bounty program covers the Quantaureum protocol end-to-end: consensus (QPOS, GM-QTD threshold signing), the QVM and QASM execution layers, the P2P networking stack, the post-quantum cryptography modules (Dilithium3, Kyber768), and the bridge. Report privately via security@quantaureum.com - never open a public issue for a vulnerability.
bug-bounty-faq-q1-title: What should a good vulnerability submission look like?
bug-bounty-faq-q1-contentPreview: Structure your report so the team can reproduce and assess it quickly
bug-bounty-faq-q2-contentPreview: In QAU, from a fixed capped fund
bug-bounty-faq-q2-content-1: Rewards are paid in QAU from the capped 25,000 QAU bounty fund (0.125% of the total 20,000,000 QAU supply, drawn from the on-chain Ecosystem Fund). Each reward draws down the balance; payouts stop once the fund is exhausted. The fund is never drawn from user balances.
bug-bounty-faq-q3-title: How fast will my report be handled?
bug-bounty-faq-q3-content-1: Acknowledgment: within 48 hours. Initial assessment: within 7 days. Fix or mitigation: depends on severity - Critical: 24h, High: 72h, Medium: 7d, Low: 30d.
bug-bounty-faq-q4-contentPreview: Yes, in release notes - unless you prefer to stay anonymous
bug-bounty-faq-q4-content-1: We follow responsible disclosure and credit reporters in release notes, unless they prefer to remain anonymous.
bug-bounty-faq-q5-title: Can I disclose the bug publicly?
bug-bounty-faq-q5-contentPreview: Only after a fix is released
bug-bounty-faq-q5-content-1: Please do not disclose the vulnerability publicly until a fix is released. We coordinate disclosure timelines with reporters.
bug-bounty-faq-q6-content-1: Issues must be previously undisclosed, reproducible, and not already known to the team.
bug-bounty-faq-q6-content-2: Rewards are upper bounds, assessed case-by-case.
bug-bounty-faq-q7-title: Where do I send my report?
bug-bounty-faq-q7-content-1: Email security@quantaureum.com with a description of the vulnerability and steps to reproduce. Do not open a public issue.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-severity-qualif: Rewards are upper bounds assessed case-by-case, paid in QAU from the capped 25,000 QAU bounty fund. Each reward draws down the fund balance; payouts stop once the fund is exhausted.
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-out-of-scope-fo: These are not included, however, we can sometimes help reach out to affected parties
page-upgrades-bug-bounty-not-included-li: Issues in third-party services not maintained by Quantaureum
Vulnerabilities already known to the team
Automated scanner reports without demonstrated impact
Missing rate limiting on public endpoints
Denial of service requiring disproportionate resources
Best-practice suggestions without a security impact
Vulnerabilities in software not in the in-scope list
